For builders

In a template, write the minus as &minus; or \2212. A chart script should format negatives itself, since a number converted to text takes a hyphen.

Rule 06.6 Balance a heading’s lines, and keep two words or more on its last line.

A heading that runs to two or more lines splits into lines of near equal length, and its last line holds at least two words. Body text wraps so its last line holds more than one short word.

Tokens

  • --oa-type-h3Inter Tight 800, 26 to 32 px, line height 1.08, tracking −1%
  • --oa-type-sectionInter Tight 800, 44 to 80 px, line height 1.03, tracking −2.5%

Why it works

Basis Design judgment

A lone word on a heading’s last line, called a widow, reads as an afterthought and pulls the eye down a line for one word. Balanced lines let a reader take in a heading at a glance.

Specifications

Headings
text-wrap: balance
--oa-type-h3
Body text
text-wrap: pretty
--oa-type-body

Related chapters

  • 02 Voice
  • 07 Layout and spacing

For builders

Older browsers ignore text-wrap and wrap as usual, so check the longest real heading at 360 px and, where a widow appears, join its last two words with a no-break space.

Rule 06.7 Hang opening quotation marks outside the text edge.

In a pull quote or a quote card, the opening mark sits in the margin, so the first letter of every line starts on the same edge. Use curly quotation marks and apostrophes (“ ” ‘ ’), and keep common ligatures on and discretionary ligatures off.

Tokens

  • --oa-type-quoteLora 400, 24 to 32 px, line height 1.3, tracking −2%

Why it works

Basis Design judgment

When the mark sits inside the edge, the first line starts a mark’s width to the right of the rest, and the block looks indented by accident. Readers know curly marks from books and newspapers, so a straight mark looks like a typing slip.

Specifications

Hang
0.39 em in Lora Italic 400, measured
--oa-type-quote
Marks
“ ” ‘ ’ (U+201C, U+201D, U+2018, U+2019)

For builders

Set hanging-punctuation: first where the browser supports it, and a negative text-indent of 0.39 em on the quote where it does not.

Rule 06.8 Set body text at 60 to 75 characters a line.

Set body text to a measure of 60 to 75 characters a line on wider screens, and intro text to 65 at most. A phone gives about 37 to 40 characters, which suits a small screen. Chapter 07 gives the column spans that deliver these measures at each width.

Tokens

  • --oa-layout-measure-body-ideal33.88rem
  • --oa-layout-measure-body-max37.37rem
  • --oa-layout-measure-intro-max41.91rem
  • --oa-type-bodyInter 400, 17 px, line height 1.6
  • --oa-type-introInter 400, 19 to 22 px, line height 1.5

Why it works

Basis Design judgment, with WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.8 (AAA, advisory)

Lines far past 75 characters make the eye lose its place on the way back to the next one. The ch unit, the width of a zero, runs wider than Inter’s average letter, so an intro set to 65ch, as in our fifth edition, measured 78 to 83 characters a line when we set it at 22 px.

Rule 06.9 Set email type in the system font stack.

Many mail apps ignore web fonts, so email sets headlines and body text in Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif, and quotations in Georgia Italic. An email is a fixed artboard 600 px wide, so it takes the scale’s phone floor sizes, as Rule 06.2 sets out. Chapter 22 shows the full template.

Tokens

  • --oa-font-family-email-sansHelvetica, Arial, sans-serif
  • --oa-font-family-email-quoteGeorgia, serif

Why it works

Basis Design judgment

A mail app that cannot load a web font falls back to a face of its own choosing, often a serif. The system stack names the fallback in advance, so every reader sees a face we chose. Our fifth edition kept this rule and then set its own email headline in Inter Tight.

Rule 06.10 Load the three faces, and let no other face stand in.

Pages load Inter Tight, Inter and Lora from their published files, in the weights the scale uses. Arial and Georgia appear only as fallbacks inside the font stacks. No other face stands in for ours, including Spectral, Source Sans, Public Sans, IBM Plex, Libre Baskerville, Playfair Display, Cormorant, Helvetica Neue for display, Times New Roman, Calibri, Roboto, Open Sans and Montserrat.

Tokens

  • --oa-font-family-display"Inter Tight", Arial, sans-serif
  • --oa-font-family-readingInter, Arial, sans-serif
  • --oa-font-family-quoteLora, Georgia, serif

Why it works

Basis Our locked identity rules; design judgment

Our locked identity rules say a font substitution is never a finished identity decision. A fallback’s one job is to keep a page readable when a font fails to load. Measured at 32 px, the heading here sets 498 px wide in Inter Tight and 504 px in Arial, 1.3 percent wider. A page that failed to load Inter Tight can look finished, and only the letters give it away. The list carries our fifth edition’s never-substitute list forward.

   This block copies, as tokens.css holds them, the custom properties chapter 06 names, every property they

:root {

  --oa-color-palette-pillar-red: #E63946;

Foundations · Chapter 07 of 28

07 Layout and spacing

Build each page on the column grid and spacing scale, readable at every width.

Every page sits on a column grid and spaces its parts in steps of 8 px. The grid changes at set window widths, called breakpoints, from 12 columns on a desktop to four on a phone, and each paragraph spans the columns that keep its lines at the measure chapter 06 sets.

A page also has to read at 320 px wide, and with its text at twice the size, with nothing cut off and no scrolling sideways.

In this chapter

  • Rule 07.1 Space everything in steps of the 8 px scale.
  • Rule 07.2 Set each page on the column grid for its width.
  • Rule 07.3 Span body text across the columns that hold its measure.
  • Rule 07.4 Set a heading closer to the text it introduces than to the block above.
  • Rule 07.5 Set breakpoints in em, so larger text gets fewer columns.
  • Rule 07.6 Make every page read at 320 px wide, with nothing lost.
  • Specifications
  • Related chapters
  • For builders

Rule 07.1 Space everything in steps of the 8 px scale.

Use the eleven steps of the spacing scale, from 4 px to 104 px, for every gap, padding and margin. Spaces around text are set in rem, so they grow with the reader’s text. The grid’s gutters and page margins stay in px.

Tokens

  • --oa-space-0500.25rem
  • --oa-space-1000.5rem
  • --oa-space-1500.75rem
  • --oa-space-2001rem
  • --oa-space-3001.5rem
  • --oa-space-4002rem

  • --oa-space-6003rem
  • --oa-space-8004rem
  • --oa-space-10005rem
  • --oa-space-13006.5rem

Why it works

Basis Design judgment

One rhythm lets the parts of different pages line up, and a reader senses the order before reading it. Every step is a multiple of 4 px, so its edges land on whole device pixels at 1x, 1.5x, 2x and 3x screen density. Our fifth edition kept the same 8 px rhythm; Edition 06 gives each step a token.

Specifications

Name a step by its multiple of 8 times 100: --oa-space-300 is 24 px and --oa-space-050 is 4 px. A value between steps means the layout is off, so move to the nearest step.

Rule 07.2 Set each page on the column grid for its width.

Lay each page on the grid for its width: 12 columns at 1440 and 1024 px, eight at 768 px and four on phones, with the gutters and margins in the specifications. Every section of a page shares the same column lines.

Tokens

  • --oa-layout-grid-wide-gutter24px
  • --oa-layout-grid-wide-margin64px
  • --oa-layout-grid-desktop-columns12

  • --oa-layout-grid-desktop-margin40px
  • --oa-layout-grid-tablet-columns8
  • --oa-layout-grid-tablet-gutter24px
  • --oa-layout-grid-tablet-margin32px
  • --oa-layout-breakpoint-wide1440px
  • --oa-layout-breakpoint-phone390px

Why it works

Basis Design judgment; our audit of the fifth edition, October 2026

When every section uses the same column lines, the eye finds the edge of each block in the same place, page after page. Our fifth edition switched among two- to six-column grids from section to section, so no column line ran the length of a chapter.

Rule 07.3 Span body text across the columns that hold its measure.

Body text spans five of 12 columns at 1440 px, seven of 12 at 1024 px, seven of eight at 768 px and all four on phones. Those spans hold the 60 to 75 characters a line that chapter 06 sets, and a block that spans more columns caps its text at the body measure.

Tokens

  • --oa-layout-measure-body-ideal33.88rem
  • --oa-layout-grid-wide-columns12
  • --oa-layout-grid-desktop-columns12
  • --oa-layout-grid-tablet-columns8
  • --oa-layout-grid-phone-columns4

Why it works

Basis Design judgment

The grid places a block, and its span keeps the lines readable. Prose run across all 12 columns at 1440 px measured 160 characters a line, more than twice the measure. Across the five-column span, the same prose measured 63.

Rule 07.4 Set a heading closer to the text it introduces than to the block above.

Leave at least twice as much space above a heading as below it. Sections part by 80 px, a label sits 32 px below the block above it and 8 px above what it names, and paragraphs part by 16 px.

Tokens

  • --oa-space-10005rem
  • --oa-space-6003rem
  • --oa-space-4002rem
  • --oa-space-2001rem
  • --oa-space-1000.5rem

Why it works

Basis Design judgment, from the Gestalt principle of proximity

Readers group what sits close together, a pattern designers call proximity. A heading with equal space above and below seems to belong to neither block, and the reader pauses to work out which one it names.

--oa-space-200
Below a label
8 px
--oa-space-100

Put the space on the heading’s own top margin, so the gap moves with the heading wherever it lands.

Rule 07.5 Set breakpoints in em, so larger text gets fewer columns.

A breakpoint is the window width where the layout changes, and an em is the reader’s text size, 16 px unless they change it. Write each breakpoint in em: 90em for the wide layout, 64em for desktop and 48em for tablet, with the phone layout as the base. On a 1440 px screen, a reader at 150 percent text gets the tablet layout and a reader at 200 percent the phone layout, with fewer, wider columns for the larger words.

Tokens

  • --oa-layout-breakpoint-wide1440px
  • --oa-layout-breakpoint-desktop1024px
  • --oa-layout-breakpoint-tablet768px

Why it works

Basis WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.4

WCAG 2.2 success criterion 1.4.4 Resize Text asks that text reach 200 percent with nothing lost. A breakpoint in px ignores the reader’s text size, so doubled text crowds a layout drawn for smaller words: five columns at 1440 px hold about 30 characters of 34 px text a line. In em, the layout steps down as the text grows, and the measure cap in rem keeps the line length.

Specifications

Wide
(min-width: 90em), 1440 px at 16 px text
--oa-layout-breakpoint-wide
Desktop
(min-width: 64em), 1024 px
--oa-layout-breakpoint-desktop
Tablet
(min-width: 48em), 768 px
--oa-layout-breakpoint-tablet
Phone
The base layout, no query
--oa-layout-breakpoint-phone

For builders

Media queries cannot read custom properties, so write the em value itself: @media (min-width: 64em). The token’s mediaQuery field in tokens.json holds each one.

Rule 07.6 Make every page read at 320 px wide, with nothing lost.

At 320 CSS px, the width of a small phone or a desktop window zoomed to 400 percent, a page shows all its content without scrolling sideways. Tables stack into one card per row. Only content that needs two dimensions, such as a wide data table or a specimen at true size, scrolls inside its own labeled frame.

Tokens

  • --oa-layout-breakpoint-phone-small360px
  • --oa-layout-grid-phone-small-margin16px
  • --oa-layout-grid-phone-small-columns4

Why it works

Basis WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10

WCAG 2.2 success criterion 1.4.10 Reflow asks for content at 320 CSS px with no loss of information and no scrolling in two directions. When we tested our fifth edition at 320 px, the page ran 524 px wide and its contrast table lost its last column.

Specifications

16 px
--oa-layout-grid-phone-small-margin

No clipped boxes and no sideways scroll at 1440 px

Foundations · Chapter 08 of 28

08 The Signal Grid

Keep the lockmark to its fixed places, and put a key beside every Signal Grid that codes content.

Democracy has a structure. The lockmark draws it as nine nodes joined by links, with the lever, a larger red node at bottom right, at the place where one change moves the rest. It sits beside the wordmark in the masthead and in a few fixed places, and its drawing never changes.

The Signal Grid uses the same nine nodes to code one thing about a piece: how far a bill has moved, which recurring series it belongs to, or which pillar it serves. A coded grid always sits beside words that say what it shows.

In this chapter

  • Rule 08.1 Draw the lockmark from its master for its size, and keep its drawing fixed.
  • Rule 08.2 Place the lockmark only in its fixed positions and sizes.
  • Rule 08.3 Set a key beside every Signal Grid that codes content.
  • Rule 08.4 Let each grid code one thing, chosen in this order: tracker progress, a series route, a pillar corner.
  • Rule 08.5 Show tracker progress with a shape for each stage, from 40 px.
  • Rule 08.6 Give each recurring series one fixed route that ends on its pillar’s corner.
  • Rule 08.7 Light one corner to name a pillar, and print the pillar’s name beside it.
  • Rule 08.8 Build the kicker from a 24 px grid, a 24 px icon and a label.
  • Rule 08.9 Keep every grid state still, and say it in words.

Rule 08.1 Draw the lockmark from its master for its size, and keep its drawing fixed.

The lockmark is a 3 by 3 grid of nodes joined around its edge and through its center, with the lever in signature red at bottom right. Place the 16 px master from 16 to 23 px, the 24 px master from 24 to 47 px and the display master, drawn for our brand guide’s fifth edition, from 48 px.

Tokens

  • --oa-color-identity-signature-on-newsprint#E63946
  • --oa-color-palette-stone#5D636D

Why it works

Basis Our measurements, October 2026

At small sizes our fifth edition’s single master lost its shape: at 24 px only 5 percent of its ink was solid, and at 16 px the lever became one pink pixel. The small masters set every node and link on whole pixels and draw the lever one size up, so it still reads as the place where one change moves the rest.

The lockmark files read --link for the links and --lever for the lever. Leave the lever on the signature token; on Prussian, place the White file. Ask the editor for the display master, which keeps our fifth edition’s drawing.

Rule 08.2 Place the lockmark only in its fixed positions and sizes.

The lockmark appears in four places, once per view: at the bottom right of social cards, covers and posters, 40 px or 0.4 in, inside the margin; beside the wordmark in L3 and L6; beside the section label on report and slide pages, 24 px or 0.25 in; and in a chart legend at 16 px, where chapter 14 calls for it.

Why it works

Basis Design judgment

A signature works by turning up in the same place, so a reader finds it without looking. Used as a bullet or scattered as decoration, it stops signing the page.

Specifications

Bottom right of social cards, covers and posters; 40 px or 0.4 in, inside the margin

Right of the wordmark in L3 and L6, 2.4 cap heights tall

Beside the section label on report and slide pages; 24 px or 0.25 in
Legend mark
16 px, in a chart legend, where chapter 14 calls for it
Favicon
Retired: favicons use ampersand B’s 16 px master (Rule 03.4)

Rule 08.3 Set a key beside every Signal Grid that codes content.

A coded grid sits beside words that say what it shows, on the same line or directly under it, at 13 px or larger: the stage and its name for a tracker, the series name for a route, the pillar’s name for a corner. Screen readers get the same words.

Tokens

  • --oa-color-text-secondary-on-newsprint#4E535B

Why it works

Basis WCAG 2.2 SC 1.1.1 and 1.4.1; Design judgment

Nine dots at 24 or 40 px cannot explain themselves, and our fifth edition’s grids coded six things with no words nearby. With the words beside it, the grid becomes a shortcut for readers who know it and hides nothing from readers who do not.

Specifications

Key
On the grid’s line or directly under it
Size
13 px or larger
--oa-type-label
Screen readers
The grid is hidden; the key’s words carry it

For builders

Write the key from the record’s data, so the words and the grid can never disagree, and mark the grid aria-hidden="true" when the key sits beside it.

Rule 08.4 Let each grid code one thing, chosen in this order: tracker progress, a series route, a pillar corner.

When a piece could carry more than one code, its grid shows the first that applies. Progress may add the stage where a reader can take part now, and a series route always ends on its pillar’s corner. A pillar corner shares its grid with nothing else. Content type is never coded by color; name it in words in the kicker.

Why it works

Basis WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1; Design judgment

Our fifth edition’s grid coded pillar, content type, progress, gaps and series on the same nine nodes, and a reader could not tell which one was in front of them. Its four content-type colors look alike in grayscale, and its Verdigris and red differ at 1.14 to 1. One code per grid, chosen in a fixed order, gives every grid one meaning.

Specifications

Order
Tracker progress, then a series route, then a pillar corner
Tracker progress
From 40 px
Series route and pillar corner
From 24 px
Content type
In words, in the kicker

Rule 08.5 Show tracker progress with a shape for each stage, from 40 px.

A tracker grid reads its nine stages left to right and top to bottom. A filled disc marks a stage done; a ring marks the stage under way; a gap, with the node and its links cut away, marks a stage that never happened; a small Stone node marks a stage not yet reached. One red disc may mark the stage where a reader can take part now. Name each stage in plain words, and say once on each tracker page what each stage means.

Tokens

  • --oa-color-graphic-essential-on-newsprint#121212
  • --oa-color-graphic-subtle-on-newsprint#5D636D
  • --oa-color-palette-pillar-red#E63946
  • --oa-color-border-strong-on-newsprint#121212

Why it works

Basis WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1; Design judgment

Shapes survive grayscale, color blindness and a cheap printer, and plain stage names let a newcomer read the key. Our fifth edition told the stage under way from a finished one by color alone, Verdigris against red at 1.14 to 1, and drew a missed stage as a dashed ring, a texture the atlas gives to a plausible link.

Give the red disc to the stage only while the reader can act, and only when no error holds the view’s red (Rule 05.3).

Rule 08.6 Give each recurring series one fixed route that ends on its pillar’s corner.

A series route runs along the links, never across a diagonal, and ends on the corner of the pillar the series serves. Six series hold six routes, and a new series takes a route no other series uses.

Tokens

  • --oa-color-graphic-essential-on-newsprint#121212

Why it works

Basis Design judgment

A route lets a regular reader spot a series at a glance, and ending on the pillar’s corner ties each series to the pillar order: Explain top left, Track top right, Connect bottom left, Act bottom right.

Rule 08.7 Light one corner to name a pillar, and print the pillar’s name beside it.

The four corners follow the pillar order in reading order: Explain top left, Track top right, Connect bottom left, Act bottom right. Light one corner as a 7 px disc at 24 px, keep the other nodes small and Stone, and set the pillar’s name beside the grid.

Tokens

  • --oa-color-graphic-essential-on-newsprint#121212
  • --oa-color-graphic-subtle-on-newsprint#5D636D

Why it works

Basis Design judgment

The pillars run Explain, Track, Connect, Act, and the corners take them in the order a page is read. Under 48 px a pillar mark sits with its word, and the corner follows the same rule.

Rule 08.8 Build the kicker from a 24 px grid, a 24 px icon and a label.

The kicker, the short line above a title, sets the grid at 24 px, 12 px of space, a Civic Line topic icon at 24 px in one color, 12 px, then its words in the label style at 13 px. The words follow Rule 01.21: the content label, then after a middle dot the series name if the piece belongs to a series, or else the topic. A record’s ID, when there is one, follows as a typed chip.

Tokens

  • --oa-size-icon-medium24px

Why it works

Basis Our 13 px floor for text; Design judgment

One definition keeps every kicker the same height and order on the site, in email and in reports. Our fifth edition defined it twice, with 20 to 24 px grids and labels at 10 and 11 px, under the 13 px floor.

Rule 08.9 Keep every grid state still, and say it in words.

Empty, loading, ready, under way and final each have their own drawing and a line of text. Nothing pulses: loading shows the links alone, with the words “Loading tracker” in a status region that screen readers announce.

Tokens

  • --oa-color-state-loading-text-on-newsprint#4E535B
  • --oa-color-state-empty-text-on-newsprint#4E535B

Why it works

Basis WCAG 2.2 SC 2.2.2, 1.4.11 and 4.1.3

Our fifth edition pulsed the lever between 20 and 50 percent opacity with no end and no pause, at 1.27 to 1.83 to 1 on Newsprint. That fails WCAG’s rules on moving content and on contrast for graphics, and the pulse told a reader nothing a word could not.

Specifications

Empty
Small nodes and links; “Nothing filed yet”
Loading
Links alone; “Loading tracker” in a status region
--oa-color-state-loading-text-on-newsprint
Ready
Stages done as filled discs; the stage in words
Under way
A ring on the current stage
Final
All nine filled
Motion
None; chapter 17 covers any change between states

Appendix · After chapter 08

Wordmark width proofs

Compare each piece at both wordmark widths at actual size, so Dustin can choose one.

Dustin Cathcart, our founder and editor, chooses the wordmark’s width from these proofs. Each proof shows one piece at actual size at today’s width and at the condensed width, both with ampersand B, set on one edge or one line so the wordmark is the one thing that changes. Today’s width stays in use until he chooses.

We recommend today’s width. At the same height the condensed drawing only runs narrower, and its heavy capitals sit close to the lettering of campaign signs. Its monogram also reads as 0&A.

The marks at a glance

The wordmark from each of its masters, the stacked lockup and the monogram, both widths at the same height.

Masthead on the site

L3 in the 1440 px site bar and L1 in the 390 px phone bar, today’s width above the condensed width on one left edge.

Masthead in email

L3 at the head of a 600 px email, the two widths side by side. A sent email carries the masthead as a PNG at twice size, with the alt text “Oath & Action”.

Avatar

The monogram, L8, on the Charcoal tile that Rule 04.7 sets as the default, in a circle and a square. A feed draws an avatar at about 32 to 48 px, where L8 at either width sets its capitals under the 14 px floor. Rule 04.7’s avatar, ampersand B alone, reads at that size and is the same at both widths, so we recommend it whichever width Dustin chooses.

Social card

The 1200 by 630 link-preview card, today’s width above the condensed width on one left edge, with its specifications under them.

Letterhead

US Letter, 8.5 by 11 inches, at true size on screen, 96 px to the inch, the two widths side by side. The print proof holds both widths, one per page, each labeled; check its scale with a ruler before you judge it on paper.

Minimum sizes at both widths

The smallest size of each mark whose size changes with the width. Chapter 03 lists today’s width alone.
